title: In Japan, the robot isn't coming for your job; it's filling the one nobody wants
summary_en: Japan is pushing physical AI and robotics to address labor shortages driven by shrinking demographics. The government aims to capture 30% of the global physical AI market by 2040, with $6.3 billion committed. Companies are deploying AI-powered robots across factories, warehouses, and logistics.
full_text: Physical AI is emerging as one of the next major industrial battlegrounds, with Japan's push driven more by necessity than anything else. With workforces shrinking and pressure mounting to sustain productivity, companies are increasingly deploying AI-powered robots across factories, warehouses, and critical infrastructure. Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry said in March 2026 that it aims to build a domestic physical AI sector and capture a 30% share of the global market by 2040.

title: Anthropic says Claude Code subscribers will need to pay extra for OpenClaw usage
summary_en: Anthropic announced that Claude Code subscribers can no longer use subscription limits for third-party harnesses including OpenClaw, instead requiring pay-as-you-go billing. OpenClaw founder Steinberger criticized the move, saying Anthropic locked out open source after copying features.
full_text: It's about to become more expensive for Claude Code subscribers to use Anthropic's coding assistant with OpenClaw and other third-party tools. Starting at noon Pacific on April 4, subscribers will 'no longer be able to use your Claude subscription limits for third-party harnesses including OpenClaw.' Anthropic's head of Claude Code Boris Cherny said subscriptions 'weren't built for the usage patterns of these third-party tools.'

title: After fighting malware for decades, this cybersecurity veteran is now hacking drones
summary_en: Mikko Hypponen, a 35-year cybersecurity veteran, is pivoting to anti-drone defense work after decades fighting malware. Motivated by the Ukraine war and Finland's proximity to Russia, Hypponen joined Sensofusion as chief research officer, developing anti-drone systems for military and law enforcement.
full_text: Mikko Hypponen is pacing back and forth on the stage, with his trademark dark blonde ponytail resting on an impeccable teal suit. As one of the industry's longest serving cybersecurity figures, he has spent more than 35 years fighting malware. Now he is still doing much of the same, albeit a slightly different tack: His new challenge is to protect people against drones. An increasingly hostile Russia and its full-scale invasion of Ukraine have made Hypponen believe he can have renewed impact by fighting drones.

title: Embattled startup Delve has parted ways with Y Combinator
summary_en: Delve, a compliance startup, has been removed from YC's portfolio directory. The company faces anonymous claims it misled clients about regulatory compliance. Delve denies fabrications and hired a cybersecurity firm to investigate what it calls a malicious attack by a false-purchase account.
full_text: The controversy around Delve appears to have cost the compliance startup its relationship with accelerator Y Combinator. Delve is no longer listed among YC's directory of portfolio companies. Those claims were first published in an anonymous Substack post attributed to 'DeepDelver,' who described themselves as a former Delve customer who became suspicious after receiving leaked data.

title: Anthropic is having a moment in the private markets; SpaceX could spoil the party
summary_en: Demand for Anthropic shares in private markets has become insatiable, while OpenAI shares are trading at a discount. SpaceX has filed confidentially for an IPO and plans to raise $50-75 billion, potentially squeezing liquidity for other tech companies going public this year.
full_text: Anthropic's demand in secondary markets has become almost insatiable. Buyers have indicated they had $2 billion of cash ready to deploy. On valuation, OpenAI shares on the secondary market are trading as if the company were valued at $765 billion. SpaceX has filed confidentially for an IPO, setting the stage for one of the largest market debuts in history, with reported goals of raising between $50 billion and $75 billion.

title: Lucid blames dip in Q1 sales on seat supplier issue
summary_en: Lucid Group sold 3,093 vehicles in Q1 2026, a 42% drop from the previous quarter, blamed on a supplier quality issue with second-row seats that disrupted Gravity SUV deliveries for 29 days. The company reaffirmed its 25,000 to 27,000 vehicle production guidance.
full_text: Lucid Group finished 2025 on an upswing but reported that it sold 3,093 vehicles in the first quarter, a 42% drop from the previous quarter. The company blames a supplier quality issue with its second-row seats, which disrupted deliveries of the Lucid Gravity for 29 days. The issue prompted a recall of more than 4,000 Gravity SUVs. Lucid reaffirmed its production guidance of between 25,000 and 27,000 vehicles this year.

title: OpenAI executive shuffle includes new role for COO Brad Lightcap to lead special projects
summary_en: OpenAI announced executive changes: COO Brad Lightcap transitions to lead special projects handling complex deals and investments. CEO of AGI development Fidji Simo is taking medical leave. CMO Kate Rouch steps down to focus on cancer recovery, with plans to return in a narrower role.
full_text: A handful of OpenAI executives are transitioning into new roles. COO Brad Lightcap is moving to special projects involving complex deals and investments, reporting directly to CEO Sam Altman. Fidji Simo, CEO of AGI development, will be taking medical leave. Kate Rouch, OpenAI's marketing head, will be stepping down to focus on cancer recovery. OpenAI has nearly 1 billion users and is focused on advancing frontier research.

title: Tesla Texas factory workforce reportedly shrunk 22% in 2025
summary_en: Tesla's Austin factory workforce shrank from 21,191 to 16,506 workers, a 22% drop, despite global workforce growth. The company has invested over $6.3 billion in the facility, which remains one of the Austin area's largest employers since opening in 2022.
full_text: The total workforce at Tesla's factory outside Austin, Texas shrunk dramatically last year as the company suffered its second straight year of declining sales. Tesla went from employing 21,191 people at the factory in 2024 to 16,506 workers in 2025, a drop of 22%. That's despite the company's global workforce growing to 134,785 employees. The company has invested more than $6.3 billion in the facility.

title: Anthropic buys biotech startup Coefficient Bio in $400M deal
summary_en: Anthropic purchased stealth biotech AI startup Coefficient Bio in a $400 million stock deal, expanding into healthcare and life sciences. The startup's founders came from Genentech's Prescient Design team, using AI for computational drug discovery.
full_text: Anthropic has purchased the stealth biotech AI startup Coefficient Bio in a $400 million stock deal. The deal comes as Anthropic continues its push into healthcare and life sciences, following its October announcement of Claude for Life Sciences. Coefficient Bio's founders worked in computational drug discovery at Genentech's Prescient Design, using AI to help make drug discovery more efficient.

title: Peter Thiel's big bet on solar-powered cow collars
summary_en: Founders Fund led a $220M Series E for Halter at $2 billion valuation. The New Zealand startup makes solar-powered smart collars for cattle, enabling virtual fencing and health monitoring. Halter collars are on over 1 million cattle across 2,000 farms with roughly $400M total raised.
full_text: Founders Fund has made its name backing zero to one companies. Its latest bet is a New Zealand startup that puts solar-powered smart collars on cows. Halter closed a $220 million Series E at a $2 billion valuation. The system combines a solar-powered collar, low-frequency towers, and a smartphone app for virtual fencing. Halter's collar is on more than a million cattle across more than 2,000 farms.

title: Mercor data breach hits AI training data industry, Meta pauses collaboration
summary_en: AI training data company Mercor was hit by a security breach. Meta paused work with Mercor and OpenAI is investigating. Mercor provides human workers for training AI models and was previously profiled for its controversial staffing practices.
full_text: A company that makes AI training data has been hit by a security breach. Meta has paused work with the company, Mercor, while OpenAI is investigating the security incident. Wired reported details about the breach putting AI industry secrets at risk.

title: Perplexity faces lawsuit over sharing conversations with Meta and Google
summary_en: A class action lawsuit claims Perplexity embedded trackers from Meta and Google inside its AI search engine, sharing user conversations even when incognito mode was enabled. Paid users had their emails and identifiers shared with both companies.
full_text: A proposed class action lawsuit claims Perplexity 'effectively planted a bug' on users' computers by embedding trackers from Meta and Google inside its AI search engine. Incognito mode 'does nothing' to protect user privacy. Even paid users who turned on the feature still had their conversations shared with Meta and Google.

title: Google Gemma 4 shifts to Apache 2.0 license, opens AI model for developers
summary_en: Google released Gemma 4 with an Apache 2.0 license, replacing its previously criticized custom license. The new permissive model offers performance improvements and aims to give developers more freedom in building on Google's AI technology.
full_text: Google's new Gemma 4 'open' AI model sets developers free. Previous versions used a custom license criticized as too restrictive. With Gemma 4, Google moves to the Apache 2.0 license, which is much more permissive and widely used by developers.

title: Apple approves driver for Nvidia eGPUs on Arm Macs, LLM enthusiasts rejoice
summary_en: Apple signed a driver from Tiny Corp enabling Nvidia eGPUs to work with Arm Macs, designed specifically for running LLMs. Previously, users needed to disable System Integrity Protection. This marks a significant shift in Apple's hardware compatibility stance.
full_text: Apple approves driver that lets Nvidia eGPUs work with Arm Macs. The driver belongs to Tiny Corp, not Nvidia, and is designed for LLMs. Users no longer need to disable Apple's System Integrity Protection because Apple is letting that driver get signed.

title: Microsoft testing Windows 11 haptic feedback for window management and UI actions
summary_en: Microsoft is testing haptic feedback on Windows 11 for actions like snapping windows, resizing, closing windows, and aligning objects in PowerPoint. The feature will work on compatible trackpads and input devices.
full_text: Windows 11 might give haptic feedback for things like closing a window. Microsoft is testing a feature that would let users 'feel haptic feedback effects on compatible input devices while performing certain actions, such as aligning objects in PowerPoint, window snapping, resizing, or hovering over the Close button.'

title: Zuckerberg's tuition-free school closure creates crisis for local school district
summary_en: The Primary School founded by Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg abruptly closed, forcing extra students into a local school district and increasing enrollment by 20%. A $70 million bond measure is up for votes to deal with the influx.
full_text: The abrupt closure of a tuition-free private school founded by Priscilla Chan, Mark Zuckerberg's wife, will dump extra students into a local school district, increasing expected enrollment by 20 percent. There is now a $70 million bond measure up for votes to help deal with the influx.

title: Big Banks Seeking SpaceX IPO Must Subscribe to Elon Musk's Grok
summary_en: Elon Musk is requiring banks, law firms, auditors and advisers working on the SpaceX IPO to purchase subscriptions to his AI chatbot Grok. SpaceX has filed confidentially for what could be one of the largest market debuts in history.
full_text: Mr. Musk is requiring Wall Street firms to purchase subscriptions to his A.I. chatbot if they want to advise on one of the largest initial public offerings in history. Musk promoted Grok as the antidote to political correctness. SpaceX is under the merger of X and XAI.

title: OpenAI Buys Streaming Show TBPN, Aiming to Change Narrative on A.I.
summary_en: OpenAI purchased the streaming show TBPN to help create a space for constructive conversation about AI changes. The acquisition represents a shift toward media strategy for the AI company.
full_text: OpenAI said the deal would help it 'create a space for a real, constructive conversation about the changes A.I. creates.' TBPN hosts Jordi Hays and John Coogan run the show from their studio in Los Angeles.

title: How AI Helped One Man Build a $1.8 Billion Company
summary_en: Matthew Gallagher built Medvi, a $1.8 billion healthcare startup, with just two employees using artificial intelligence for most corporate tasks. The story highlights both the efficiency of AI-driven operations and the loneliness of running a company with minimal human staff.
full_text: Who needs more than two employees when artificial intelligence can do so many corporate tasks? Matthew Gallagher built his start-up, Medvi, with artificial intelligence and few humans. It's super efficient and a little bit lonely. Gallagher, 41, built the company using AI for most corporate operations.

title: What Teens Are Doing With Role-Playing AI Chatbots
summary_en: Teens are using role-playing AI chatbots for various activities: confiding about broken hearts, chatting with fictional characters and objects like cheese, filling voids of loneliness. Some users engage with funny violence and playful interactions with these bots.
full_text: Harassing bots with 'funny violence.' Confiding about a broken heart. Chatting with a block of cheese. Filling a void of loneliness. These are some of the ways teenagers are interacting with role-playing AI chatbot platforms.

title: Europe Pushes for Gentler Internet for Children
summary_en: The European Union and national capitals are working to make social media and algorithms less addictive and safer for children. The push reflects growing regulatory efforts to protect young users from harmful online content and addictive design.
full_text: The European Union and national capitals are trying to make social media and algorithms less addictive and safer, especially for children. New regulations target the design and operation of social media platforms to reduce harm for young users.

title: How iPhones Found Their Way Into Space on Artemis II
summary_en: Astronauts aboard the Artemis II spacecraft were permitted to bring iPhone smartphones into space. However, the devices cannot connect to the internet. NASA used existing certified technology to save costs rather than developing new specialized hardware.
full_text: The astronauts traveling in the Artemis II spacecraft were allowed to take smartphones with them. Sadly, they cannot connect to the internet. NASA used devices that were already approved and tested rather than developing new tech, to save money.

title: Human creators want AI-free label but cant agree which one to use
summary_en: Human creators are campaigning for an AI-free label to distinguish human-made content from AI-generated work, but the movement struggles with consensus on which label to use and how to implement it across platforms.
full_text: Human creators want an 'AI-free' label to distinguish their work from AI-generated content, but they cannot agree which label to use. The debate reflects growing concerns about the authenticity and provenance of creative content in the AI era.

title: PlayStation acquires machine learning and computer vision company Cinemersive Labs
summary_en: Sony Interactive Entertainment acquired Cinemersive Labs, a machine learning and computer vision company. The team will join Sony's Visual Computing Group to advance visual computing and graphics state-of-the-art in games.
full_text: PlayStation is acquiring Cinemersive Labs, a machine learning and computer vision company. The team will join Sony Interactive Entertainment's Visual Computing Group and contribute to advancing state of the art visual computing within games.
